narrative.title: The Mirror-Wing Kite Test
narrative.scenario: A kite maker balances a two-wing kite and demands true mirror symmetry: the left wing's every fork must reflect the right wing's — left arms matching right arms, values identical at mirrored joints. Before the kite flies, one check certifies the whole frame as aerodynamically balanced or flags it for rebuild.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the tree is a mirror image of itself around the root, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: Both wings fork identically with mirrored values 3 and 4.
Both 3s hang on the same side of their wings — not mirrored.

hintLevels: Level 1: Symmetry is a comparison between the two wings, not a traversal of one.
Level 2: Compare in mirrored lockstep: wing-one's left against wing-two's right, and vice versa.
Level 3: The null algebra mirrors the Same Tree pattern; anchor the check on the root's two children.
